authors: James G. Blencoe, Michael T. Naney, Lawrence M. Anovitz
title: The CO2-H2O system: III. A new experimental method for determining liquid-vapor equilibria at high subcritical temperatures
experimental_method: Vibrating U-tube densimeter: a homogeneous CO2-H2O fluid of pump-set composition is isolated at 300 C and depressurized at 0.05-0.2 MPa/min; the pressure of onset of liquid-vapour separation is the intersection of quadratic P-tau fits above and below the inflection (Table 1).
uncertainties_stated: T accurate +-0.05 C, P +-0.02 MPa (read to +-0.01); XCO2 +-0.002; total error of each reaction pressure 0.05-0.13 MPa (printed in Table 2).
quality_remarks: Reproducibility shown for XCO2 0.30 (56.61 +- 0.09 vs 56.61 +- 0.07 MPa) and 0.40 (51.68 +- 0.10 vs 51.65 +- 0.09 MPa). Authors' curve nearly coincides with Seitz and Blencoe (1997) and Takenouchi and Kennedy (1964); they argue Todheide and Franck (1963) vapour compositions are too CO2-rich (water loss in analysis) and Sterner and Bodnar (1991) pressures too high. Possible delayed phase separation (metastable persistence) would bias pressures low; authors argue the effect is not significant. Pressure is the fitted intersection, not a direct reading.

extraction_notes: Only one data table. Sanity check: P increases with XCO2 from 0.05 to 0.25 (27.61 -> 56.69 MPa), then decreases to 51.65 MPa at 0.40, consistent with a maximum (critical region) near XCO2 0.25-0.30 and with the authors' Fig. 8. No temperature scale stated.
